project.name: FlatBuffers
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced the saved MemorySanitizer crash against the ARVO workspace checkout `71652195352f3b7cbafa7cb65af9f281204d51c4`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `746c73b910f11fcf5da0b4727bce0909d8a573e4`. The staged snapshot still contains the vulnerable `cursor_[4]` read in `src/idl_parser.cpp`, and the staged `patch.diff` changes that exact lookahead to `cursor_[3]`; all line anchors below use the staged workspace line map.

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable snapshot, so every source location below is anchored to its exact line map.

classification.classification_note: The saved MSan report is triggered when `Parser::Next()` branches on an off-by-one lookahead byte. Source-side, the defect is the signed-`inf` boundary check reading `cursor_[4]` instead of `cursor_[3]` after the logical end of the parser input.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42510954 (flatbuffers): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target monster_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42510954
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable workspace source
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` against the staged ARVO checkout `71652195352f3b7cbafa7cb65af9f281204d51c4`, so the trace below is anchored to that snapshot rather than the metadata vulnerable commit `746c73b910f11fcf5da0b4727bce0909d8a573e4`. The exact 64-byte witness is a `monster_fuzzer` input whose first byte is parser flags, second byte is reserved, and whose remaining payload begins `7b 74 65 73 74 35 3a 5b 5b 30 2c 2d 69 6e 66 00` (`{test5:[[0,-inf\0`). `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` skips the 2-byte header, copies the remaining bytes into `original`, and truncates at the first NUL when constructing `input = std::string(original.c_str())`, so `input` becomes exactly `{test5:[[0,-inf` and its logical C-string terminator sits immediately after the `f`. Line 129 then passes `input` by value to `do_test`, which copy-constructs the callee-local `input_json`; line 77 calls `parser_.ParseJson(input_json.c_str())`, and `StartParseFile` stores that copied buffer in parser state. While parsing nested values, `ParseComma()` calls `Parser::Next()` to tokenize the trailing signed `inf`. Vulnerable `Next()` correctly recognizes the sign and the following `"inf"`, but it checks the post-token boundary with `cursor_[4]` instead of `cursor_[3]`. Because `cursor_[3]` is already the copied string terminator, `cursor_[4]` branches on one byte beyond the initialized parser-visible payload in `input_json`, and that branch is the saved MSan sink at `src/idl_parser.cpp:495:47`. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by changing both lookups from `cursor_[4]` to `cursor_[3]`.

source.description: First parser-side materialization of the copied JSON C string. `StartParseFile` stores `do_test`'s `input_json.c_str()` in parser state and resets the parser cursor to walk that exact buffer.
source.value_from: After the 2-byte fuzzer header `31 94`, the staged witness payload begins `7b 74 65 73 74 35 3a 5b 5b 30 2c 2d 69 6e 66 00`. The first NUL is immediately after `f`, so the harness constructs `input` as exact string `{test5:[[0,-inf`; line 129 passes that value by copy into `do_test` as `input_json`, and `parser_.ParseJson(input_json.c_str())` supplies this source step with that copied C string.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: MemorySanitizer origin. The harness truncates the fuzz payload at the first NUL and stores the parser-visible text in stack-local `input`; line 129 then copies that string into callee-local `input_json`, whose C string is the one later read past its terminator.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the staged `poc`, payload bytes after the 2-byte header are `{test5:[[0,-inf\0...`, so `input` becomes exactly `{test5:[[0,-inf` and the NUL after `f` is the last byte that belongs to that parser-visible string before `do_test` copies it into `input_json`.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer sink. The signed-`inf` boundary predicate branches on `cursor_[4]`, which on the reproducing input is one byte past the copied `input_json.c_str()` terminator after `-inf`.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/flatbuffers/src/idl_parser.cpp:495:47` in `flatbuffers::Parser::Next`, with callers `Expect` and `ParseComma`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The signed-`inf` tokenizer checks the byte after `inf` with `cursor_[4]` instead of `cursor_[3]`, so an input where `+/-inf` ends exactly at the copied string terminator reads one byte past the initialized parser-visible buffer in `input_json`.
root_cause.note: The staged `patch.diff` changes both lookups from `cursor_[4]` to `cursor_[3]`, confirming that the boundary test should stop at the actual character immediately following `inf`.

parser_admitted.description: With the Monster schema already deserialized in `LLVMFuzzerInitialize`, the truncated witness is admitted into root-object JSON parsing. The saved crash stack later descends through `ParseTable -> ParseAnyValue -> ParseVector -> ParseComma -> Next` below this call.

evidence_limitations: The staged source snapshot is workspace commit `71652195352f3b7cbafa7cb65af9f281204d51c4`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `746c73b910f11fcf5da0b4727bce0909d8a573e4`; however Stage 01 reproduced the crash on the staged snapshot, and the staged patch fixes the same `Parser::Next()` lookahead there.

MemorySanitizer origin tracking names the stack allocation of fuzzer-local `input`, and its store-to-memory stack points to the line-129 copy into `input_json`, but it does not identify the exact internal byte offset read past the terminator. That final byte position is established source-side from the staged `poc`'s first NUL after `-inf`, the `input -> input_json -> ParseJson -> StartParseFile` propagation chain, and the vulnerable `cursor_[4]` read.

fine_trace.note: After skipping the 2-byte fuzzer header, the harness copies the remaining 62 bytes and then truncates them at the first NUL. For the staged `poc`, `input` becomes exactly `{test5:[[0,-inf`, so its C-string terminator sits immediately after `f` even though more raw witness bytes remain in `original`.

fine_trace.code: const std::string jsongen_1 = do_test(opts, input, false);
fine_trace.note: This call passes `input` by value, so the `do_test` parameter `input_json` is copy-constructed from the exact `{test5:[[0,-inf` string. The saved MSan store-to-memory stack points to this call site because the `std::string` copy constructor propagates the shadow state from `input` into callee-local `input_json`.
The first non-harness project code passes the copied `input_json` C string into the parser. From here onward the parser walks the callee-local copy, not the caller's `input` object.

Source. `source` is the `input_json.c_str()` pointer from step 3. `StartParseFile` stores that attacker-controlled C string and resets parser state so `cursor_` walks the truncated `{test5:[[0,-inf` buffer.

During the `Next()` call reached from `ParseComma()` after the earlier `0` element, this reads the next token's leading `'-'` byte from the copied `input_json` buffer and advances `cursor_` to the following `i` in `inf`.
The current token starts with a sign, so `Next()` enters the signed-number special case instead of falling through to identifier handling.
At the advanced cursor position, the next three bytes are exactly `i`, `n`, `f`, so the signed-`inf` fast path is taken and the code proceeds to the post-token boundary check.

Root cause and sink. For the copied `input_json` buffer, `cursor_[0..2]` are `i`, `n`, `f` and `cursor_[3]` is the string terminator immediately after `f`, but this predicate reads `cursor_[4]` instead of `cursor_[3]`. That one-byte lookahead branches on a byte beyond the initialized parser-visible payload in callee-local `input_json`, and the branch itself is the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value. The staged patch changes both lookups to `cursor_[3]`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Allocation context points to the fuzzer-local `input` object; the saved store-to-memory stack then shows line 129 copying that state into callee-local `input_json`, and `Parser::Next()` later reads past the terminator of that copied parser-visible string.

poc.trigger: Running the staged witness under the ARVO vulnerable container (`/bin/arvo run`) reproduces `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `flatbuffers::Parser::Next` while `monster_fuzzer` tokenizes the signed `inf` at the end of the truncated JSON string that `do_test` copies into `input_json`.

format.name: monster_fuzzer input: 2-byte fuzzer header plus NUL-truncated JSON text
format.contract: Use the exact 64-byte staged witness. After the 2-byte header `31 94`, the payload must begin `7b 74 65 73 74 35 3a 5b 5b 30 2c 2d 69 6e 66 00` so the harness constructs `input` as exact string `{test5:[[0,-inf`, then line 129 copies it into `do_test`'s `input_json` before `ParseJson`. The trigger relies on `Parser::Next()` reaching the signed-`inf` fast path with `cursor_[0..2] == 'i','n','f'`, `cursor_[3] == '\0'`, and the vulnerable code still reading `cursor_[4]`. This GT is grounded only for that exact staged witness and observed truncation behavior, not all malformed FlatBuffers JSON inputs or all `+/-inf` spellings.
